learning_outcomes.text: Provide insight into the design of high-frequency systems.
Utilize microstrip technology to design filters and amplifiers at high frequencies.

syllabus_topics: Transmission lines: equivalent circuit, reflections, open and short-circuited lines, VSWR, impedance
High-frequency filters: Butterworth, Chebyshev, conversion to normalized filters and denormalization, microstrip filters
Electro-Magnetic Compatibility (EMC): what it is, practical application
Calculation of a Butterworth and Chebyshev low-pass filter with a cutoff point at 500MHz. Simulation of this design
Conversion of this filter into microstrip technology and simulation. Measuring and analyzing existing designs using the spectrum analyzer
Calculation of an HF amplifier using S-parameters. This amplifier is built and measured with the spectrum analyzer

assessment_methods.method: Oral exam with written preparation for Theory
Oral exam with prior preparation of a workpiece for Lab (second attempt)

assessment_rules: If less than 5/20 is obtained on one of the course components, the maximum score for the course unit is 9/20, meaning failure. For RF Technology: Theory, the first and second exam chances are oral exams with written preparation. For RF Technology: Lab, the first exam chance is based on assignments, and the second exam chance is an oral exam with prior preparation of a workpiece. Partial transfers for successful results (YT5917 - RF Technology: Theory and YT5918 - RF Technology: Lab) are possible within and across academic years.
